source_title: Harleian MS 279 in Two Fifteenth-Century Cookery-Books
attested_pattern: Two coordinated operations precede one final object; the same recipe then resumes it by pronoun and same-broth wording.
gdt595_relevance: A short action chain can plausibly share a right-edge object, and immediate same-object continuation is genre-normal.
transfer_limit: This supports constituent order and anaphora only; it does not identify any Voynich root or object class.

attested_pattern: A singular portion-of-rice measure is followed by plural pronouns referring to the rice itself.
gdt595_relevance: A measure or fill phrase need not become the continued patient; AIIN can remain medium while another referent supplies the object.
transfer_limit: This analogy does not prove that AIIN is a measure or that the omitted patient is a body.

attested_pattern: An introduced food object is carried through long paratactic preparation chains by repeated pronouns.
gdt595_relevance: Leftward same-segment participant reuse and German derselbe/dieselbe realization are historically natural.
transfer_limit: The text is earlier and culinary; it supplies a workshop-language analogy, not a cipher key.

attested_pattern: Precisely weighed ingredients are combined and subsequently handled as one batch.
gdt595_relevance: Weight or quantity information can coexist with a separately tracked batch referent.
transfer_limit: This is an operational analogy only; no Voynich substance, weapon, or genre identity follows.

attested_pattern: The manuscript contains medical recipes and bathing instructions close to the target date, with explicit referent changes in procedural prose.
gdt595_relevance: A real medical/bathing witness near 1420 makes imperative chains, containers, applications, and marked patient changes historically available comparison classes.
transfer_limit: The catalogue establishes date and contents; it does not match any Voynich passage or validate the German working translations.
